handoff.notes:
## Goal

Give the training lanes a write-only HTTP route, `POST /api/stats/dev-records`, that files development game records exactly as `jackioh-server stats-import` does, behind its own optional bearer token (`STATS_INGEST_TOKEN`), with its own 1 MiB body cap. Switch `training/loop.sh` from `DATABASE_URL` plus `cargo run -p jackioh-server` to posting finished days (and, on the gather lane, each fresh batch) with `curl`. Record the rules decision as ruling `R1023000` with its proving tests. `stats-import`, `import_dev_records`, the store, and the client stay unchanged.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/src/config.rs` | change | Add `DEV_RECORDS_MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 1_048_576` beside `API_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, commented with the R1023000 marker and the ~550-record note. Do not add it to `tests/export_config.rs` (allowlist; it stays server-only). |
| `crates/server/src/env.rs` | change | Add `pub stats_ingest_token: Option<String>`; parse like `parse_github_issues_token` (trimmed, blank is unset); redact in `Debug` as the issues token is; append `"STATS_INGEST_TOKEN"` to `SERVER_ONLY_ENV_VARS`. |
| `crates/server/src/api/http.rs` | change | Add `AuthLevel::Ingest`; add `pub raw_body: Option<String>` to `Req`; give `read_body_text` a `cap: usize` parameter (its one caller `read_body` passes `API_MAX_BODY_BYTES`); add the Ingest branch to `run_route` (step 4); update the two `Req` literals. |
| `crates/server/src/api/stats.rs` | change | Add `pub async fn post_dev_records(app: &Arc<App>, req: Req) -> ApiResult` calling `crate::cli::import_dev_records::import_dev_records` unchanged (step 5). |
| `crates/server/src/app.rs` | change | Add `("POST", "/api/stats/dev-records", AuthLevel::Ingest, h!(api::stats::post_dev_records))` after the `PUT /api/stats/player` entry. |
| `Cargo.toml`, `crates/server/Cargo.toml` | change | Add `subtle = { version = "2.6.1" }` to workspace dependencies (matches `Cargo.lock`) and `subtle = { workspace = true }` to the server crate, for the constant-time token compare. |
| `crates/server/tests/api/stats.rs` | change | Add `mod r1023000_dev_records_route` with a raw-body POST helper and eight tests (see Tests). |
| `training/loop.sh` | change | Rewrite `import_records`, add `post_records`, post the gather batch in `gather`, update the header comment and the Environment list: no `DATABASE_URL`, no `cargo run -p jackioh-server` (steps 7–8). |
| `training/README.md` | change | The gather lane steps, Setting it up, and the Where-the-numbers-go table: post instead of `stats-import`/`DATABASE_URL`. |
| `training/gather.md` | change | `imported.txt` line: days already posted when the box has the token, not loaded with `DATABASE_URL`. |
| `crates/server/README.md` | change | Environment table row for `STATS_INGEST_TOKEN`; HTTP surface row for the route; body-cap sentence naming both caps. |
| `docs/deploy-cloudflare.md` | change | Step 3 secrets: `wrangler secret put STATS_INGEST_TOKEN` for staging, generated with `openssl rand -hex 32`, plus the production note for step 6. |
| `spec/09-architecture.md` | change | §9.11 Sources sentence: a development record enters only through `stats-import` or this route, with a `[[R1023000]]` link. |
| `spec/rulings/R1023000.md` | new | The ruling (step 9). |
| `spec/pending/1023.md` | new | The §11 paragraph in the shape of the current `spec/pending/*.md` files. |

Do not touch: `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`, `crates/shared`, any migration, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `apps/web` (including `serverConfig.ts`), `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/11-rulings.md`. Governing spec: §9.11 (Sources, Totals, Queries, publication gate), R378, R654, R1044000; CLAUDE.md rules 3 (ruling mechanics) and 9 (named constants).

- What changed:
- - Server: new `AuthLevel::Ingest` and `POST /api/stats/dev-records` (`crates/server/src/api/http.rs`, `app.rs`). The handler (`api/stats.rs`) calls `import_dev_records` unchanged, so R378's refusals hold exactly. New optional `STATS_INGEST_TOKEN` (`env.rs`, redacted in `Debug`, listed in `SERVER_ON…
- - Lanes: `training/loop.sh` gains `post_records` (splits each file with `split -C 900000`, posts pieces with `curl --fail --data-binary` + bearer header) and `import_records` now posts finished days; the gather lane also posts each batch right after appending it. No `DATABASE_URL`, no `jackioh-serv…
- - Docs: `training/README.md`, `training/gather.md`, `crates/server/README.md` (env row, route row, both body caps), `docs/deploy-cloudflare.md` (staging secret + fresh production token).
- - Spec: `spec/rulings/R1023000.md`, `spec/pending/1023.md`, §9.11 Sources names both entries. `stats-import` stays untouched.
- How tested (commands I ran, what they printed):
- - `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::stats::r1023000` — 8 passed, 0 failed (404 unset; 401 missing/wrong/user token; 400 live-source and bad-id with nothing written; `{read:3,written:3,skipped:0}` then `{read:3,written:0,skipped:3}`; over-cap 400 "too large"; dev games count on `?sour…
- - `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::stats` — 54 passed, 0 failed.
- - `cargo test -p jackioh-server` — 100 + 6 + 2 + 1658 + 691 passed, 0 failed (2 ignored are the pre-existing `daily:` marks).
- - `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean. `cargo fmt --check` — clean. `sh -n training/loop.sh` — passes.
- - `cargo jackioh spec check` — "1888 rulings, 4895 proofs, 61337 citations in 3985 files, 25086 links: ok".
- Decisions the issue did not settle (alternative rejected):
- - `parse_stats_ingest_token` duplicates the issues-token parser's body under its own name (rejected: reusing a github-named parser for another variable).
- - `gather` posts the fresh batch only when both variables are set (rejected: the plan's bare call, which would log a curl failure every cycle on an unconfigured lane).
- - Step 6 mints a fresh production token instead of copying staging's (rejected: shared secret couples revocation).
- - README body-cap sentence uses 131,072 bytes — the code sets `API_MAX_BODY_BYTES = PLAYER_STATS_BYTES_MAX`, not the issue's stale 64 KiB.
- Reviewer, look twice at: the held-401-then-counted ordering in `run_route` (mirrors the bad-user-token path so floods still burn address budget); the 404-before-limiter for the unset token (matches unknown-path behavior exactly); `curl` posts the token only in a header with stdout discarded, never …
- Gaps: `shellcheck` is not installed on this box, so `loop.sh` has `sh -n` only — it uses POSIX constructs alone (no `local`, no bashisms). People's part after merge (token generation, Render/Cloudflare secrets, box drop-ins, service restart) is not in this build, as the issue says.

## Goal

The 30 Mythics and 20 printed-Mythic tokens each get a **diorama**. All of those tokens' pictures have landed. Each diorama is one file per card in `apps/web/src/cards/art/dioramas/<set>/`, holding 5–8 slices cut from the painter's still picture (base and Radiant). The slices stand at depths, some are bent, and two or more run the card's own idle loop.

Wherever a face drew depth planes, it now draws the diorama:
- A drag turns it up to `DIORAMA_TURN_MAX_DEG` (25°) in inspect, the hover preview, the Collection and full screen.
- The loop runs in hand, inspect and on the board, inside the motion slots.
- The takeover flies through the slices.
- Under reduced motion it stays flat.

## Risks

- **A normal picture or a repaint moving.** Only the `#alt` seed reads an alt recipe (`sceneRecipeOf`, unchanged), and the normal recipe files stay untouched. R3401000's tests catch any change.
- **Shared tests.** Any test that reads all of `ALT_SCENE_RECIPES` breaks unless filtered as in step 7. Grep for `ALT_SCENE_RECIPES` again before stopping.
- **The 0.6 share.** Meditative's pale paper makes this the hardest rule to meet. Measure and retune; never lower the constant.
- **Gold or bytes.** A part's default paint can fall in the gold window, or high counts can push past the byte ceiling. The tests name the part: repaint it or drop a count.
- **Presentation only** (CLAUDE.md rule 7). The recipes are static data read by card id, so there is no hidden-information or determinism risk. `card-versions.cy.tsx` checks `meditative-042`, whose Alt art now only differs more from its normal one.

- **Three new kit parts**, because #3396 rejected stand-ins. Rejected: a bench standing in for the sofa, and a figure's `item-oar` for the oar.
- **Close existing parts used as is:**

- **Family `meditative`, with one red seal on every Alt picture**, rather than another family.
- **Skies share no colour with the normal ones**, as in #3396, rather than differing in hue or composition alone.
- **0.6 is measured in Cypress**, not in vitest, because jsdom cannot paint.

## Goal

Each seat's own view carries the engine's `combat_forecast` of its attacks. That covers:
- every practice snapshot;
- the 1v1 seat `view` frame;
- the Duos seat `view` frame.

A watcher's view never carries it.

While an attacker is selected or dragged, each legal target with a forecast entry shows one small chip:
- the damage dealt;
- the damage taken back (unit targets only);
- ☠ on whichever side dies;
- a struck-through `DS` when a Divine Shield breaks.

A setting, "Show attack outcomes" (on by default), hides the chips. Lessons draw no chip, and the coach is unchanged. A new ruling, R3477000, amends R3100000. The owner asked for "pretty unintrusive": the chip shows only while aiming, takes no click and moves no layout.

- `apps/web/src/game/Game.hiddenDrain.test.tsx`: `it("R3497000 a hidden board shows a new view's long batch at once with End turn enabled")`; `it("R3497000 a tab that turns visible with steps queued shows the newest view at once")`; `it("R3497000 a board without drainWhenHidden, a replay, or a visible tab behaves as before")`. ## Done when

- [ ] Hidden online board shows a new view's long batch at once with End turn enabled.
- [ ] Becoming visible with steps queued shows the newest view at once.
- [ ] Visible tab unchanged; existing animation tests pass unmodified.
- [ ] Flushed burst ending with the seat's turn start sends the turn-start cue.

## Risks

- Throttled-timer tests: fake timers plus an injected source keep the new tests deterministic; no test touches real `document.visibilityState` except via the existing `setVisibility` helper, and the new tests prefer injection.
- `drain()` also fires `onSettled` → `setShown(latest)`, which is exactly what enables `legal`; the `drain` signal clears `FxLayer`/`AuraLayer` state as the existing hand-over drain does, so no new visual path is invented.
- Reduced-motion bursts run synchronously with nothing queued, so `drain()` is a harmless no-op there; the drain leaves reduced-motion, showcase, and chat paths untouched.
- Log completeness: draining skips animation entries, never events; the game log joins view windows independently of the queue.

None.

When a host's clock cuts a decision short, its finalists are still scored after the opponent's reply on every sampled world (#3498).

- **Callback.** `AiOptions.wrap_up` stops only the beam's slice of the counter. The beam's open lines then end their turn, and the reply and the other worlds run on to `should_stop`.
- **Share.** `AI_WRAP_UP_SHARE` (0.6). Every host with a clock fires the wrap-up at that share of its limit: the wasm module (practice AI, dungeon fights through the practice driver, browser bots), the ladder bots and the Duos AI team.
- **Report.** `SearchStats.replied`, `.worlds_scored` and `Decision::fell_short()`, printed by `think` and the timing gate.

## Risks

- **Permit lifetime.** The permit must move into the blocking closure, not the async fn. Otherwise a dropped request frees the permit while the fold still runs.
- **Dropped first request.** If the first request of a match is dropped mid-fold, its result is lost and the next open folds again. It still waits for the permit, so it is bounded. Note this in R3500000.
- **Flight cleanup.** `strong_count <= 2` is only valid because clones are taken under the `flights` lock. Keep that lock's scope tight, with no `.await` while it is held. Clippy's `await_holding_lock` would flag it.
- **Unavoidable behaviour change.** A claim in flight now holds a seed slot. A deliberate burst is refused as 409 (the message is unchanged), and an honest player's single claim is unaffected.
- **Postgres.** The count is an edit to a query, so the Docker suite proves it. The fake and Postgres definitions must match: `claim is not null and settled_at is null`.
- **Sweep skip.** The skip is per process. During a deploy handover two processes could still both settle a claim, and `economy_practice_seed_settle`'s "only where unmarked" already makes the pay land once.
- **Duos wiring.** The Duos permit use is covered by the shared `open` tests and the existing Duos replay tests. Review it by reading the diff.
- **Contracts.** The server README's route table is the contract and must change with the behaviour. Cached pages, the per-account `REPLAY_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE` limit and seat filtering (CLAUDE.md rule 7) are untouched.

- [ ] Hidden time is not counted, and time before `pagehide` is.
- [ ] After a reload `RunTimer` shows the kept total.

## Risks

- **Resurrecting a settled run.** A pause that rewrote `DUNGEON_RUN_KEY` for a finished run would pay it again on reload. `setSession` returns early for finished runs, and a test covers it.
- **Stale snapshot.** The first render loads with no subscriber, so the clock starts only in `subscribe`; the store commits there. A timer frame at most can lag.
- **Unclean exit.** A crash with no `pagehide` loses the time since the last save. That undercounts and never overcounts; accepted.
- **Two tabs on one run.** Each tab banks its own session and the later write wins. It is rare and undercounts; not handled.
- **Storage.** No `DUNGEON_STORAGE_VERSION` bump, because a bump would drop every kept run. `elapsedMs` is optional on read.
- **Test reloads.** `reload()` calls `cleanup()`, which pauses and banks time up to the current clock. Tests that move the clock to model a closed page must dispatch `pagehide` first.
- **Purity.** No crate changes; the generated `wire/` has no diff.

**Decisions the issue left open**
- *Start screen:* counts while the Dungeon page is open, including the start screen's Continue wait. Rejected: pausing it until Continue, which would wire `DungeonPage`'s `entered` state into the store.
- *Leaving the page:* time stops when the Dungeon page unmounts, so the "Back to Play" link, the primary leave path, stops the clock. Rejected: only hide and `pagehide`, which would time a tab left open on another route.
- *`startedAt`:* kept in storage, removed from `Dungeon`. Rejected: reusing it as a "virtual start".
- *`pageshow`:* also resumes the clock, for a back-forward-cache restore.

## Open questions

None block the build. The maintainer may prefer the start-screen wait or the Campaign's server-checked runs (§15.12) handled differently. The issue says the second "Patch" suggestion, "a dungeon run in progress survives a card patch", also edits `KeptRun`, so build the two in turn.

## Goal

`Scenario` (`crates/engine/src/testkit/scenario.rs`) gains five queries, each with its own tests in the kit:
- `events_of(kind)` and `count(kind)`, since setup;
- `last_events_of(kind)` and `last_count(kind)`, over the last step;
- `offered(seat)`, the seat's legal actions.

Every card-test copy of `count`, `fired` or `events_of` whose behaviour is exactly one of these is deleted, and its calls move to the kit. Every copy of `fn count(`, `fn fired(`, `fn events_of(` or `fn offered(` that stays gets one line saying how it differs. Only test code and docs change. So `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main` reports kind Internal, and `cargo test -p jackioh-cards` passes the same number of tests.

"Exact" means all three of:
- the same source: `events()` or `last_events()`;
- a filter on the event type alone;
- the same result: `usize`, or a typed `Vec<GameEvent>`.

Whether the kind is spelled as a `&str` or a `GameEventType` doesn't matter. Nor does how the type is read: `event_type()`, `matches!` on the variant, or `js(..)["type"]`.

I checked every body and call site at base `a52cde4f26`:
- **Exact (28 copies in 28 files):** 22 of the 24 `count`s, 4 of the 16 `fired`s and 2 of the 11 `events_of`s.

handoff.notes:
**Goal**

Add two optional `Handicap` fields to the engine, both proven by ruling R3582000:
- `fewer_opening_cards` (`fewerOpeningCards`) takes cards off a seat's opening draw, which is §2.1's entry plus `extraOpeningCards`. The hand never drops below `MIN_OPENING_HAND` (1), and the mulligan works on that smaller hand.
- `draw_every` (`drawEvery`) lets a seat take its R183 start-of-turn draws only on its own turns whose `turns_started` is a multiple of n (n=2: its 2nd, 4th, 6th turns). On the other turns it draws nothing at the start of the turn: no card, no fatigue step, no cast on draw. A card's own "draw" still draws.

`createGame` refuses `fewerOpeningCards < 0` and `drawEvery < 1`, and the message names the field. A field that is absent, or set to 0 or 1, is neither stored nor serialized, so every existing game, tier, lesson, golden trace and fuzz seed is unchanged. `Handicap.ts` is regenerated. The ruling note, its tests in `handicap.rs` and its pending paragraph are added.

# Plan (opus, strong)

**Goal.** Make `e2e/cypress/component/fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx` pass 4/4 in `e2e component (chrome)` by fixing what the product spends its frames on. Every moment at 390x844, 360x780 and 844x390 must hold a mean frame ≤ `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS` and a worst frame ≤ `FX_PHONE_FRAME_WORST_MS` in at least one of `FRAME_ATTEMPTS` plays, under the unchanged 4x throttle (R3351000, R2803000). The spec prints every sample before it asserts, and the other component specs stay green.

The planner profiled the cast locally (Cypress 16.1, Chrome 156, 4x). The machine reproduces CI: the cast ran 550–1000 ms mean with 2–5 frames per window. Three product causes were measured, and fixes 1 and 2 were emulated in the browser:

1. **`:has()` whole-subtree invalidation.** `board.css` has `.app-shell--wide:has(> .game) > *` and `… > :not(.game)`, a universal compound after `:has()`. They make Blink invalidate the whole `.app-shell`/`.game` subtree on every effect the director mounts. Each read that follows then forces a full-document style recalc of about 1,140 elements, about 110 ms at 4x, several times per frame. 2. **Board relayouts cost about 180–200 ms each (4x).** Even a 1 px change, toggling `.board`'s `translate` for the shake, or a hand reflow (`useHandSpring`'s `offsetLeft`) triggers one. The cause is the phone rule `.lane { grid-template-rows: repeat(4, minmax(var(--card-h), 1fr)) }` together with `.zone { container-type: size }`. With explicit row lengths, `repeat(4, max(var(--card-h), calc((100% - 3 * var(--gap)) / 4)))`, the same relayout takes 0–1 ms. That formula changed the zone boxes from 69x91 to 69x94, though, so the exact equivalent has to be derived.
